conditional_setup: In a single fixed exact representation, suppose a predetermined local family of present inequalities depends on exactly two retained physical coordinates z=(f,p) after all fixed coordinates have been substituted. No row may contain an unaccounted coordinate, including the scalar outside its justified zero face.

Require that four protected present unary rows provide finite lower and upper bounds for both coordinates. These rows remain retained throughout. conditional_construction: Enumerate intersections of each unordered pair of nonparallel boundary lines using exact rational two-by-two determinants. Keep only intersections satisfying every row of H exactly. No numerical tolerance or approximate-zero test is used.

With the protected finite rectangle and the full-dimensional premise, these points are precisely the vertices of P, possibly with duplicate representations. A source boundary supporting two distinct feasible vertices contains a polygon edge. Retain one deterministic lowest-original-ID row per coincident facet halfspace, together with all four protected unary rows.

For each omitted nonconstant row, choose a vertex maximizing its linear functional among the enumerated vertices. The normals of the two retained adjacent facet rows r,s generate the outward normal cone there. Hence a_i=lambda*a_r+mu*a_s with lambda,mu>=0; boundary cases allow one multiplier zero. The supporting value satisfies lambda*b_r+mu*b_s<=b_i.

Save those two source premise IDs, the two exact nonnegative multipliers and the exact nonnegative RHS slack. A constant omitted row requires its own exact tautology check. Neither missing targets nor missing premises count as deletions.

An independent auditor needs no polygon enumerator: check all coordinate identities and RHS inequalities, all nonnegative multipliers, source-row associations, unchanged copied rows and that every premise is in the FINAL retained set. This prevents mutually circular simultaneous deletions.
